title: Georgia's 5th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Georgia's 5th Congressional District, based in Atlanta and parts of DeKalb and Clayton counties, pits incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative Nikema Williams against Republican challenger John "Bongo" Salvesen in a rematch of the 2024 contest. Williams, who succeeded civil rights icon John Lewis in 2020 and served as chair of the Democratic Party of Georgia until 2025, is heavily favored in this safely Democratic district. The race takes place against the backdrop of Georgia's high-profile Senate and gubernatorial contests and will test Democratic turnout in a key metro Atlanta seat.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this specific general election race. The Cook Political Report rates the district as "Solid Democratic."

candidates.name: Nikema Williams
candidates.summary: Nikema Williams is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2020 after succeeding the late Congressman John Lewis. She previously served in the Georgia State Senate and chaired the Democratic Party of Georgia from 2019 to 2025. Williams serves on the House Financial Services Committee and is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, Progressive Caucus, and New Democrat Coalition.

career_history.title: Chair
career_history.description: First Black woman to chair the state party; resigned in March 2025

career_history.title: Georgia State Senator
career_history.description: Elected in special election after Vincent Fort resigned

candidates.name: John "Bongo" Salvesen
candidates.summary: John Salvesen, also known as "Bongo," is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 5th Congressional District, running unopposed in the May 2026 primary. He is a handyman by trade and previously challenged incumbent Nikema Williams in the 2024 general election, receiving approximately 14% of the vote. Limited public biographical information is available about his background and policy positions.

forecast.rationale: Georgia's 5th Congressional District is a safely Democratic Atlanta-anchored district (Cook Political Report: Solid Democratic). Incumbent Nikema Williams (D) is the successor to John Lewis, served as chair of the Georgia Democratic Party until 2025, and has held the seat since 2020. Republican challenger John "Bongo" Salvesen lost to Williams by a massive margin (~86% to ~14%) in the 2024 rematch of this same matchup. No public polling exists for this race, which tempers confidence, but the district's strong Democratic lean, the incumbent's political stature, and Salvesen's poor 2024 performance all point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage. Expected margin is consistent with the 2024 result adjusted for a midterm environment.
